title: Grass-silage wash-count and hydraulic-pressure response data (Tables 1–2)
description: Transcribed treatment means and SEM from the conference-proceedings Tables 1–2, plus the reported experimental context. This is a reference dataset, not an activated process parameter table.
persistent_identifier: Grassland Science in Europe, volume 17, pages 450-453 (2012); stable publisher PDF URL supplied
source_title: Investigating the effects of hydrothermal conditioning, detergent and mechanical pressing on the isolation of the fibrous press-cake fraction from grass silage
authors: C. King; J. McEniry; P. O'Kiely; M. Richardson
publisher: European Grassland Federation, Grassland Science in Europe, volume 17
source_location: Printed pages 451–452, Methods, Tables 1–2, and footnotes; official proceedings PDF pages around 473–475
license: Proceedings identify copyright as Polish Grassland Society 2012, all rights reserved. Confirm redistribution terms before broad publication; source URL and citation are retained.
applicability: Laboratory study of ensiled forage, not fresh roadside grass. Experiment 1 used perennial ryegrass and cocksfoot; Experiment 2 used Italian ryegrass and timothy. Experiment 2 used 200 g silage samples, 1–3 repeated washes, and a hydraulic press at 1.5, 3.0, or 4.5 MPa. It does not establish screw-press performance, roadside contaminant removal, or a GreenHub yield factor.
conversion_and_scaling: Numeric values are transcribed without unit conversion. DM is reported as g/kg press cake; NDF is g/kg DM. Table 2 values are aggregate treatment means across species/harvest factors. SEM values are copied from the table; they are not converted into standard deviations or confidence intervals.
uncertainty: Triplicate field plots are described; response means and SEM are reported. The accessible table does not provide raw replicate values. Table 2 calls one response 'proportion of solubles removed' while its footnote defines it as solubles in press-cake relative to the starting silage; that definition conflict is preserved and blocks using the response as a recovery coefficient. P-value row effect scope is not explicit in the table.
provenance_note: Measured literature evidence for technology comparison only. No GreenHub default or route activation was changed. A paired fresh-roadside-grass trial is still needed for the GreenHub press model.
